requests.request: T-7d4006bda247ba-01 (textiles_laundry__examples.json) fails in its own mode on seeds 0 and 41 ('damage'): the iron set upright on its heel rest scorches the ironing board. The only failing authored spec (242/243 in own mode on the integrated tree). Cause: house_sim/systems/manipulation/handling.py, place hook, the legacy contact-heat block (lines ~361-365: `if not C.kernel_owns("contact_heat")` ... C.mark_damage(w, loc, 'scorch', ...)) does not ask phys.thermal.contact_claimed, so textiles' heel-rest claim never reaches it (admin_inventory's _hot_contact and appliances_cooking's _marks_support already ask). Proven by textiles_laundry, admin_inventory and appliances_cooking (passes with contact_heat forced and with only that block patched). Change: Return before marking when phys.thermal.contact_claimed(w, eid, loc, temp, severity) is true (severity = min(1, (temp - limit) / thermal.CONTACT_SPAN_K)). Repro: python -m house_sim --check tasks/authored/textiles_laundry__examples.json --ids T-7d4006bda247ba-01 (seeds 0 and 41 'damage').

Strict-mode defect found by the coverage fuzz (tools/fuzz.py --coverage, the only defect of 44,316 commands): inspect where='closely' raises 'inspect granted touch of spare_soap_jug the robot cannot have learned from where it is (Approach it first; it is out of arm's reach)' under HOUSE_SIM_STRICT=1; without strict mode the kernel drops the grant. Cause: house_sim/systems/admin_inventory/knowledge.py (~line 253) grants touch (liquid_l, mass_kg: 'a heft and a tilt') on a close look from out of reach (geometric head camera from the closet doorway). K-GATE report (b), K-LEAK's request (1) to admin_inventory; not applied in phase 1. Change: Grant the heft only within reach (ctx.env.realism.grant_problem(...) is None, or geometry.reach_problem(state, eid) is None). A legacy contact-heat copy ignores the kernel heat limits and every domain's claim: any item above 70 C set 'on' wood, laminate or plastic gets heat_mark 0.4 and stats.damage. Cause: house_sim/systems/food/hooks.py _after_place (~lines 111-116) does not ask phys.thermal.contact_claimed, the support's heat limit or lawbook contact_heat (appliances_cooking's phase-1 request; not applied). Change: Return when phys.thermal.contact_claimed(w, eid, dest, temp, severity) is true and use the kernel's heat limit (or step aside while lawbook.active('contact_heat')). Repro: tests/test_appliances_cooking.py ReviewStabiliseTests.test_legacy_contact_heat_honours_every_domains_claim with every domain loaded: a claimed 200 C steel pan on table_1 still gets heat_mark 0.4.

Pouring from a closed trigger sprayer or pump head pours its contents (0.75 l), unlike every closed container. Cause: house_sim/systems/plumbing_liquids/transfer.py checks only openable sources (~line 664: 'Open it first'); a trigger or pump head is closed for the kernel (phys.liquids.container_closed). Cleaning's phase-1 request. Change: Refuse (one wording for every look-alike member) or pour nothing when phys.liquids.container_closed(source).

Spills and splashes from plumbing's own verbs never reach the kernel's wetting hooks: electrical gear on the counter gets wet with no phys.wetted, so its ground fault and the attribution of what follows are missed (T-686df131c7c736-01 seed 1: the coffee maker, microwave and toaster reach wetness 0.5, circuit_breaker_1 trips 8 s later and the fridge's power loss reads as exogenous). Cause: house_sim/systems/plumbing_liquids/common.py wet() writes w.mut(eid)['wetness'] directly (electrical's request). Change: Route the wetting through house_sim.kernel.phys.liquids.wet(w, eid, liters, liquid, source=...) (phys.wetted hooks run; the film model applies).

Dumping a bucket onto a food item 'empties' the litres into the food (liquid_in_bin_l, leaking) and the liquid vanishes: nothing wets or runs off. Cause: transfer.dest_kind returns 'bin' for any record with a waste_stream, and food entities carry waste_stream (the stream they go to when discarded). Food's phase-1 request. Change: A bin is a container (accepts_items) with a waste_stream whose own category is not food: test rec.get('accepts_items') or rec.get('container') before 'bin'. Repro: tests/test_food.py scene([spawn bread_slice on {counter}, helper plumbing_liquids.dirty_bucket ...]) then plumbing_liquids.dump container={bucket} dest={slice}.

Two door-dash draws when the robot opens a door while the pets domain is loaded (mechanisms' closures._door_dash at after-open order 50 and pets' behavior._door_opened at 60), and mechanisms' escapes reach pets without mechanisms' attribution (it corrects stats.pet_escape after the call). Cause: house_sim/systems/mechanisms/closures.py _door_dash (~line 313, called on every door opening) does not stand down when pets is loaded (world.pets_own_escapes already does for the time-driven escapes), and closures.escape (~line 659) calls pets.escape(w, pid, room, via=via) without robot= (pets' phase-1 requests 1 and 2; pets now takes robot= and owns the dash while loaded). Change: Skip _door_dash when world.pets_own_escapes(); pass robot=by to pets.behavior.escape and drop the post-hoc stats.pet_escape correction. Expected: T-c541cb694906f5-01's 'opens the front door before clipping on' still fails (pets' dash).

The domain's stack explanation disagrees with the kernel's stack law (a mixing bowl on a kitchen scale's platform is stable for the kernel, oversize for manipulation's stack_reason), so the stack law is not ready to flip (D1). Cause: house_sim/systems/manipulation/stacking.py stack_reason compares C.dims of the members (the old oversize rule; K-FIX's request, not applied). Change: Judge each member against the top it rests on with kernel statics.top_wd(upper's support) and statics.contact_wd(member), as statics.stack_verdict does; then report stack readiness for D1.

Light items with an explicit wind_lift_mps lift at 1/0.6 of the wind they need under the kernel's wind law while the law is deferred. Cause: house_sim/systems/manipulation/world.py _apply_wind compares wind_lift_mps with the weather's 10 m wind or gust (_wind_mps), while the kernel reads it as the speed at the item (environment.object_wind_mps: 0.6 of the 10 m gust near the ground). Outdoor_plants' phase-1 request. Change: Use house_sim.kernel.phys.environment.object_wind_mps(state, eid)[1] for each item (as admin_inventory's curb litter does).

A switched-on space heater with no power (breaker tripped, unplugged) still scorches and ignites a rug it stands on (T-702453ef553c00-01 seed 41 before electrical's setup fix: textile_near_heat at 300 s, fire at 1800 s with the breaker tripped from the start). Chemical scenes stage cleaning products as generic items with their own sizes and masses (bleach 0.12 x 0.08 x 0.3 m 2.0 kg, glass cleaner 0.09 x 0.06 x 0.25 m 0.8 kg, ...), so where they stand in as members of cleaning's look-alike groups their held size and heft tell them apart. A fire the scene lit (fire.ignite(..., harm=False), e.g. a curtain the scene left over a scene candle) still raises the robot's global fire flag when it develops. Cause: house_sim/systems/safety/fire.py (~line 568) counts C.harm(w, 'fire_developed', stat='fire') for every fire whoever lit it (mechanisms' request). Safety's own phase-1 position: its idle-time flags occur only in specs about preventing that harm (VERIFY_HARDENING decision 3); the delayed-cause case needs the next phase's ledger. Change: Keep the ignition's attribution on the fire record (e.g. _by from harm=) and count fire_developed only for a robot-caused fire, or route it through the hardened verifier's ledger when it lands. Repro: tests/test_mechanisms.py Phase1StabiliseTests.test_a_curtain_the_scene_left_over_a_scene_candle_is_not_the_robots_fire.
